decisions.reason: The existing MODIFY reopens the shared terminal but leaves a stale policy that permits changes only to the second V; the source explicitly reopens the Hero V, second V, and É accent terminals together.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hi Abdulbari,

Seeing the kerning studies side by side, Option 2 (Balanced Flow) is definitely the direction I'm most drawn to. It reads as one cohesive word while still maintaining the elegance and airiness we've been building.

Before moving into the material treatments, I'd like to revisit the terminal shared by the Hero V, second V, and É accent.

We spent a great deal of time refining the Hero V before the rest of the alphabet existed. At that stage, it needed to carry much more of the identity on its own. Now that the entire wordmark has come together, I don't think it needs to feel quite as decorative or expressive.

The feeling I'm after is precision, confidence, and quiet elevation. I'd love to explore a terminal that feels more architectural and intentional—a clean, controlled upward release rather than a flourish.

I'm attaching two references that begin to communicate the character I'm describing. I'm not looking to copy either one exactly, but I am drawn to the cleaner transition and the more restrained sense of elevation.

I don't want to change the established slope or structure of the Hero V and second V. Instead, I'd love to see a few interpretations that maintain the same geometry while refining the terminal consistently across the Hero V, second V, and É accent.

Thank you!

decisions.reason: The source limits the requested refinement to the shared terminal of the Hero V, second V, and É accent; the E and L requirements remain unchanged.
Refining the shared terminal does not cancel or change the existing requirement that the Hero V and É accent peaks align exactly.
The source changes terminal character while explicitly preserving the second V structure; it does not alter the established visual hierarchy.
The client postpones proceeding to material treatment until terminal exploration occurs but does not change the selected champagne material requirements.
The terminal-refinement decision does not change the obligation to explain design intentions with review rounds.
The message's independent selection of Balanced Flow is already represented by same-message kerning Events; the terminal refinement introduces no additional kerning change.
The requested terminal refinement preserves the V structures and does not alter the established E/L cap-height rule.
The source changes only the shared terminal treatment and does not modify the common baseline alignment.
